misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: VaR fails the subadditivity condition for asymmetric return distributions, meaning the VaR of a combined portfolio can actually exceed the sum of individual VaRs, penalizing diversification ([fact-02]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: The square-root-of-time rule assumes i.i.d. normal daily returns with zero mean; when markets exhibit volatility clustering, regime persistence, or serial autocorrelation, the rule significantly underestimates multi-day tail risk ([fact-08]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: VaR completely ignores the magnitude of losses beyond the confidence cutoff; rogue traders can exploit this blind spot by writing deep OTM puts that show zero VaR violations until an extreme tail event causes insolvency ([fact-10]).

The sorted scenario losses reveal that the 5th worst loss (99% 1-day VaR) is $253,385, and the 5 worst losses are $253,385, $260,110, $275,420, $301,200, and $320,905.

coreTakeaways: Value at Risk quantifies maximum expected loss at confidence level X, but fails subadditivity as a coherent risk measure ([fact-01], [fact-02]).
Expected Shortfall (CVaR) directly measures the severity of catastrophic tail losses and forms the core of the Basel FRTB regulatory framework ([fact-03], [fact-04]).
Historical simulation combined with volatility updating (Hull-White) and rigorous 250-day Basel backtesting provides robust institutional risk oversight ([fact-05], [fact-09], [fact-11]).
